title: Sections vanishing on a closed subscheme
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a proper $k$-scheme, $\mathcal L$ an ample invertible sheaf on $Y$, and $Z\subset Y$ a closed subscheme. For all sufficiently large $n$, the kernel $V_n$ of $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal L^{\otimes n}|_Z)$ generates $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ on $Y\setminus Z$, and the associated morphism $Y\setminus Z\to\mathbf P(V_n)$ is an immersion.
Here properness, ampleness, invertibility, and schemes are understood in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-sc-ample], [def-sc-invertible-module], with generation by sections as in [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], the associated morphism to $\mathbf P(V_n)$ (over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, with coordinates indexed by a basis of $V_n$) as in [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections], and immersions as in [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].

proof.text: Put $U=Y\setminus Z$. By [def-sc-ample], choose $r\ge1$ and a closed immersion $j:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ with $\mathcal L^{\otimes r}\cong j^*\mathcal O(1)$. The current blueprint definition permits any such embedding. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible], $\mathcal L^{\otimes r}$ is absolutely ample. It follows directly from [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] that $\mathcal L$ is absolutely ample: a section of $(\mathcal L^{\otimes r})^{\otimes d}$ is a section of $\mathcal L^{\otimes rd}$ with exactly the same affine nonvanishing open, and the quasi-compactness condition is unchanged. Tensor reassociation is checked on local rank-one bases.

The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$), and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the one-point affine Noetherian scheme. Properness implies finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $Y$ Noetherian. Let $\mathcal I$ be the quasi-coherent ideal of $Z$ given by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. The sheaf $\mathcal O_Y$ and each $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$, $d\ge0$, are quasi-coherent of finite type: invertibility means locally free of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module], and powers are invertible [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. They are coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Apply part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] to the quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_Y$; thus $\mathcal I$ is coherent and, by the same equivalence, finite type.

For each $d\ge0$ identify $V_d$ with $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d})$. Indeed, on an open trivializing $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$, a section is $a e$, and its restriction to $Z$ is zero exactly when $a$ lies in the ideal of $Z$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Thus multiplication embeds $\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ into $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ with precisely the restriction kernel; these descriptions agree on overlaps, hence also on global sections. On opens disjoint from $Z$, that ideal is $\mathcal O$ since restriction to the empty scheme is zero. Consequently $(\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d})|_U=\mathcal L^{\otimes d}|_U$. This uses only the local free rank-one description [def-sc-invertible-module], not exactness of tensoring with an arbitrary module.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation] with the absolutely ample $\mathcal L$ and the finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal I$. Choose $a\ge0$ such that $\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ is generated by finitely many global sections for every $d\ge a$. Restricting its evaluation surjection to $U$ and using step 3 shows that $V_d$ generates $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}|_U$. Also [lem-pc-coherent-hi], with $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, coherent $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ and $i=0$, gives finite-dimensional $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L^{\otimes d})$. Its subspace $V_d$ is finite-dimensional.

For $n\ge a$, choose a basis of $V_n$ and restrict its sections to $U$. They still generate: every section in $V_n$ is a constant linear combination of the basis, so their stalk spans coincide. The associated $k$-morphism $\varphi_n:U\to\mathbf P(V_n)$ is [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections], where projective coordinates are indexed by sections, as in Tag 0FD5. A basis change is justified by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points]: if $b_i=\sum_j a_{ij}c_j$, the linear forms $\sum_j a_{ij}T_j$ generate $\mathcal O(1)$ because the inverse matrix expresses every $T_j$ in their span. They therefore define a projective coordinate map. The inverse matrix defines its inverse, since their composites pull back every $T_i$ to itself and uniqueness identifies the composites with identity. The same uniqueness rewrites $\varphi_n$ in the new basis. Thus any nonzero $s\in V_n$ may be taken as a basis coordinate. Write $D(s)$ for that standard affine chart. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-morphism-chart-preimage], $\varphi_n^{-1}(D(s))=Y_s$ and every ratio $v/s$, $v\in V_n$, pulls back to the ratio of the corresponding sections. The assertion for arbitrary $v$ follows by its linear expression in that basis. If $U$ is empty, use the unique morphism from the empty scheme (including $\mathbf P(0)=\varnothing$); it is an immersion since it identifies the empty closed subscheme. Hence assume $U$ nonempty below, so $V_n\ne0$.

Put $n_0=a+r$ and fix $n\ge n_0$. Let $t_0,\ldots,t_N\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L^{\otimes r})$ be the pullbacks by $j$ of the projective coordinates. Their nonvanishing opens cover $Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]. For any $x\in U$, choose $s_1\in V_{n-r}$ nonzero at $x$, using step 4 and the generation criterion [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre]; choose $j_0$ with $t_{j_0}(x)\ne0$. For each $i$, put $v_i=s_1\otimes t_i$. Its restriction to $Z$ is zero, so $v_i\in V_n$. Tensor products and their restrictions are compatible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2). Put $s=v_{j_0}$. The fibre formula in part (3) of that node shows $s(x)\ne0$ and $Y_s=Y_{s_1}\cap Y_{t_{j_0}}$: a tensor of two vectors in one-dimensional vector spaces over a field is nonzero exactly when both vectors are nonzero. In particular $Y_s\subset U$.

Work with this pair $(s_1,t_{j_0})$. On $D(s)\subset\mathbf P(V_n)$, the ratios $v_i/s$ are regular functions by the standard-chart description [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]: expand $v_i$ in a basis of $V_n$ containing $s$, so each ratio is a linear combination of chart coordinates and $s/s=1$. The target chart $D(T_{j_0})\subset\mathbf P^N_k$ has polynomial coordinate ring $k[T_i/T_{j_0}:i\ne j_0]$ by part (c) of that same node. Send $T_i/T_{j_0}$ to $v_i/s$. The universal property of a polynomial ring extends these assignments uniquely to a $k$-algebra homomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], it defines a $k$-morphism $q:D(s)\to D(T_{j_0})$.

Let $h:Y_s\to D(s)$ be the restriction of $\varphi_n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-morphism-chart-preimage], the pullback by $qh$ of $T_i/T_{j_0}$ equals $(s_1\otimes t_i)/(s_1\otimes t_{j_0})=t_i/t_{j_0}$. For the equality, trivialize both invertible factors over $Y_s$ by $s_1$ and $t_{j_0}$; the equality is then $1\cdot c/1=c$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts](b), these are exactly the coordinate pullbacks of $j|_{Y_s}:Y_s\to D(T_{j_0})$. Both maps are over $k$, and the coordinates generate the polynomial $k$-algebra. The bijection [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] therefore gives $qh=j|_{Y_s}$.

The map $j:Y_{t_{j_0}}\to D(T_{j_0})$ is a closed immersion: it is the base change of the fixed closed immersion $j$ along the chart inclusion, by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). The inclusion $Y_s\to Y_{t_{j_0}}$ is an open immersion. Open and closed immersions are immersions by [def-weil-closed-immersion] (use an identity for the other factor); composition preserves immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). Hence $qh=j|_{Y_s}$ is an immersion. Apply [lem-zl-immersion-cancellation] to $h$ and $q$ to conclude that $h$ is an immersion. This avoids adding a separate affine-ring factorization lemma.

For every $x\in U$ step 6 produced an $s=s_1\otimes t_{j_0}$ with $\varphi_n(x)\in D(s)$. Thus the family of these target opens covers $\varphi_n(U)$. Steps 5 and 9 say that on the full inverse image of every such open the induced map to it is an immersion. Apply [lem-zl-immersion-near-image-locality] to conclude that $\varphi_n$ is an immersion. Step 4 already gives generation, and $n\ge a+r$ guarantees both $n\ge a$ and $n-r\ge a$. This proves both assertions for every $n\ge n_0$.
